About Lithuania Overview

MBBS in Lithuania

Lovely Lithuania, a Northern European Baltic State bordering Latvia, Belarus, Poland, and the Baltic Sea, is known for its rich history, advanced infrastructure, excellent education, and top medical colleges—making it a popular destination for medical students.

The capital city, Vilnius, is a cultural, educational, and innovative center. The nation has a strong economy, dominated by the technology, manufacturing, and education sectors. Lithuania is also a member of the EU and the Schengen Area, so it is very convenient for international students to travel throughout the rest of Europe.

Apart from educational excellence, Lithuania also offers a quality of living at a reasonable cost. Living in Lithuania as a medical student is nice, with cheap public transport, affordable accommodation, and a secure environment. The welcoming environment and cosmopolitan culture make it an ideal destination.

All Requirements for MBBS in Lithuania

Understand the essential criteria and requirements

Ensure your eligibility for pursuing MBBS and starting your medical journey.

Eligibility Criteria to Apply

To secure MBBS admission in Lithuania, students must meet the following criteria:

  • Completion of 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology.
  • Minimum marks: at least 50% in PCB (40% in SC/ST/OBC categories).
  • NEET Qualification: Mandatory for Indian candidates practicing in India.
  • English proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) is sometimes a requirement by specific universities.

Required Documents & Intake

The MBBS admission in Lithuania typically has two major intakes: September (Fall Intake) and February (Spring Intake). Most medical schools receive most applications for the September intake. Early application is recommended.

Documents Needed:

  • 10th and 12th mark sheets.
  • Valid passport (validity of at least two years).
  • NEET Scorecard & Passport Size Photographs.
  • IELTS/TOEFL Certificate (if required).
  • Medical Certificate & SOP/CV.

Cost of Study in Lithuania

€7K - 12K
Annual Tuition Range A budget-friendly option for international students.

The MBBS in Lithuania is comparatively less expensive than in most Western nations. MBBS typically costs between €7,000 and €12,000 per year, depending on the institution. Unlike private medical colleges in India, MBBS does not entail the payment of capitation charges and donations.

Campus Life & Living Expenses

Cost of Living €400 to €700 per month.

It is simple and inexpensive to live in Lithuania as a medical student. Universities provide campus hostels, but private apartments can be rented as well (average price €150 to €400 per month). Indian food shops and outlets can be easily found.

The public transport is affordable and efficient. A public transport pass for a month is available for around €15 to €20. Campus life is marked by cultural events, sporting events, and student clubs that give campus life a vibrant feel.

Pathway Particulars

Duration & Structure

The MBBS follows the pattern of medical education in Europe and typically runs for six years. The Pre-Clinical Stage (First 3 Years) is focused on theoretical topics, and the Clinical Phase (Last 3 Years) involves practical training, clinical rotations, and internships.

Medium of Teaching

The medium of teaching is mainly English. All the major medical schools offer MBBS courses in English, enabling a trouble-free learning process. Students can also study elementary Lithuanian to communicate with patients during clinical training.

MBBS Admission In Lithuania

A step-by-step roadmap to admission

The admission process generally begins 6 to 8 months before the intake, so early application is recommended in order to book a seat.

  1. Fill out the admission form: Visit our official website and complete the MBBS admission form.
  2. Verification: The university will verify your application form, along with uploaded documents.
  3. Screening: The university undertakes a screening process to determine eligibility.
  4. Visa Process: Apply for a student visa to the nearest Lithuania Embassy or Consulate, attaching confirmation of admission. Simple visa procedures are a strong advantage.
  5. Enrollment: Receive a hard copy of the admission letter, travel to Lithuania, and complete enrollment.

Scholarships for MBBS in Lithuania

Many institutions and entities provide scholarships for international students.

  • Lithuanian State Scholarships: Offered by the government.
  • University-Specific Scholarships: Merit-based or need-based.
  • Erasmus+ Scholarships: Funded by the EU, offering financing and exchange opportunities.
  • Other Courses: Besides MBBS, study Dentistry, Pharmacy, Nursing, or Biomedical sciences.

Career Opportunities After MBBS

Career opportunities after MBBS in Lithuania offer varied career prospects globally.

  • Practice in Europe: Sit for licensing examinations and practice in Lithuania or any country in Europe.
  • Practice in India: Indian students can appear for the FMGE to practice in India.
  • Postgraduate Studies: Specialize in areas such as surgery, cardiology, or research through MD or PhD programs.
  • Hospitals & Teaching: Jobs in public/private hospitals or become faculty members.
MBBS in Lithuania Syllabus

Comprehensive medical curriculum

The well-planned programs equip the students with both theoretical training and practical skills.

Pre-Clinical Phase (Years 1–2)

Anatomy, Physiology, Biochemistry, Histology, Embryology, Genetics, Medical Biophysics, Cell Biology, Human Ethics & Professionalism, Introduction to Clinical Practice.

Para-Clinical Phase (Years 2–3)

Pathology, Pharmacology, Microbiology, Immunology, Medical Psychology, Public Health, Behavioral Sciences, Medical Statistics, Epidemiology.

Clinical Phase (Years 4–6)

Internal Medicine, General Surgery, Obstetrics & Gynecology, Pediatrics, Orthopedics, Dermatology, Ophthalmology, ENT, Psychiatry, Neurology, Cardiology, Pulmonology, Oncology, Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine, Radiology, Anesthesiology, Infectious Diseases.

Internship (Final Year)

Internal Medicine, Surgery, Gynecology & Obstetrics, Pediatrics, Emergency & Critical Care, Primary Care (Family Medicine), Community Medicine, Elective Rotations.
